```{r prep, include = FALSE}
### Format tables in both HTML and Word, without format-specific markup
make_table <- function(x, caption) {
  ft <- flextable::flextable(x)
  ft <- flextable::theme_booktabs(ft)
  ft <- flextable::bold(ft, part = "header")
  ft <- flextable::align(ft, align = "left", part = "all")
  ft <- flextable::set_caption(ft, caption = caption)
  flextable::set_table_properties(ft, layout = "autofit", width = 1)
}

### Set counters for numbering tables and figures
table_number <- 0
figure_number <- 0

### Helper functions for figure and table numbering
next_table_caption <- function(caption){
  table_number <<- table_number + 1
  paste0("Table S", table_number, ". ", caption)
}

next_figure_caption <- function(caption){
  figure_number <<- figure_number + 1
  paste0("Figure S", figure_number, ". ", caption)
}


### Function to extract and format optimism metrics table for a given gender
internal_table <- function(gender_in) {
  ### Read in the already calculated optimism results
  optimism_results <- readRDS("data/p5/optimism_adjusted_performance_metrics.rds")$results
  ### Check for required variables
  required <- c("Gender", "Analysis", "Subgroup", "N", "Metric",
                "Apparent performance (median)", "Optimism-adjusted performance",
                "Optimism 2.5th percentile", "Optimism 97.5th percentile")
  if (!all(required %in% names(optimism_results)))
    stop("Missing optimism result column(s): ",
         paste(setdiff(required, names(optimism_results)), collapse = ", "))
  ### Extract results for correct gender
  x <- optimism_results[optimism_results$Gender == gender_in, required, drop = FALSE]
  ### Format variables
  x$Analysis <- factor(x$Analysis, levels = c("Overall", "Ethnicity", "Age Cat", "Region"), labels = c("Overall", "Ethnicity", "Age", "Region"))
  x$Metric <- factor(x$Metric, levels = c("ICI", "E50", "E90", "Discrimination"))
  x <- x[order(x$Analysis, x$Subgroup, x$Metric), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(x) || anyNA(x$N)) stop("Missing N for ", gender_in)
  data.frame(
    Analysis = as.character(x$Analysis),
    Subgroup = as.character(x$Subgroup),
    N = format(round(x$N), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE),
    Metric = as.character(x$Metric),
    Apparent = sprintf("%.3f", x[["Apparent performance (median)"]]),
    `Optimism-adjusted` = sprintf("%.3f", x[["Optimism-adjusted performance"]]),
    `Optimism (p2.5 - p97.5)` = sprintf("%.3f - %.3f",
                                        x[["Optimism 2.5th percentile"]], x[["Optimism 97.5th percentile"]]),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}

### Read in and format temporal validation table (metrics)
temporal_table <- function(gender_in, interventional = FALSE) {
  summary_file <- if (interventional)
    "data/p5/temporal_validation_interventional_performance_metrics.rds" else
    "data/p5/temporal_validation_performance_metrics.rds"
  if (!file.exists(summary_file)) stop("Missing summary: ", summary_file)
  x <- readRDS(summary_file)$tables_3dp[[gender_in]]
  if (is.null(x)) stop("Missing ", gender_in, " table in ", summary_file)
  expected <- c(if (interventional) "Risk factor", "Follow-up index (years)", "Prediction interval", "N",
                "ICI", "E50", "E90", "Discrimination")
  if (!identical(names(x), expected))
    stop("Unexpected columns in ", summary_file, " for ", gender_in)
  x[["Follow-up index (years)"]] <- as.integer(x[["Follow-up index (years)"]])
  for (metric in c("ICI", "E50", "E90", "Discrimination"))
    x[[metric]] <- sprintf("%.3f", x[[metric]])
  x
}

### Read variable groups
var_binary <- readRDS("data/p5/var_binary.rds")
var_poly <- readRDS("data/p5/var_poly.rds")

### Calendar time is also presented with the continuous predictors
var_cont <- c("caltime", var_cont)

### Filename separator used by p2_assess_nonlinear.R
nonlinear_savename <- "_"
```

This document presents outcome incidence rates, shape of the non-linear effects of variables, internal validation and optimism-adjusted results, instability results, and temporal validation results.

# Cardiovascular disease incidence rates

## By year

Annual incidence rates were calculated in the complete development cohort, separately for the female and male models. Event free follow-up was split across calendar years, from start of ofllow-up until the first cardiovascular event or censoring. For each calendar year, the total number of cardiovascular events is divided by the total event free follow-up time. Rates are expressed in per 1,000 person-years..

```{r annual-incidence}
outcome_incidence_by_year <- readRDS("data/p5/outcome_incidence_by_year.rds")
make_table(outcome_incidence_by_year, next_table_caption("Annual cardiovascular outcome incidence rates."))
```

## By outcome type

Incidence rates in the entire cohort, stratified by outcome type: primary care, hospital episode statistics (seondary care), office for national statistics (death).

```{r type-incidence}
outcome_incidence_all <- readRDS("data/p5/outcome_incidence_all.rds")
outcome_incidence_primary <- readRDS("data/p5/outcome_incidence_primary.rds")
outcome_incidence_secondary <- readRDS("data/p5/outcome_incidence_secondary.rds")
outcome_incidence_ons <- readRDS("data/p5/outcome_incidence_ons.rds")
make_table(outcome_incidence_all, next_table_caption("Overall incidence rates, all outcome types."))
make_table(outcome_incidence_primary, next_table_caption("Overall incidence rates, primary care."))
make_table(outcome_incidence_secondary, next_table_caption("Overall incidence rates, secondary care."))
make_table(outcome_incidence_ons, next_table_caption("Overall incidence rates, cvd-related death (ONS)."))
```

# Shape of non-linear predictor effects and interactions with age

The following figures show the fitted nonlinear effects and interactions with age in the final female and male models. Age was modeled using restricted cubic splines with knots at 25, 40, 57.5 and 75 years. Other continuous variables were modeled with three knots at default locations (10th, 50th and 90th percentile). These are the shapes resulting from the model fitted on imputation chain 1.

## Interaction with binary predictors

These plots show how the hazard ratio for each binary predictor varies over different ages.

**`r next_figure_caption("Age interaction with binary predictors.")`**

```{r nonlinear-binary, out.width='25%', fig.show='hold', fig.align='default'}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(paste0("figures/p5/model_assess_nonlinear",nonlinear_savename,var_binary,".png")), rel_path = FALSE)
```

## Interaction with polytomous predictors

These plots show how the hazard ratio for each polytomous predictor varies over different ages.

**`r next_figure_caption("Age interaction with polytomous predictors, female model.")`**

```{r nonlinear-polytomous-female, out.width='33%', fig.show='hold', fig.align='default'}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(paste0("figures/p5/model_assess_nonlinear",nonlinear_savename,"2_",var_poly,".png")), rel_path = FALSE)
```

**`r next_figure_caption("Age interaction with polytomous predictors, male model.")`**

```{r nonlinear-polytomous-male, out.width='33%', fig.show='hold', fig.align='default'}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(paste0("figures/p5/model_assess_nonlinear",nonlinear_savename,"1_",var_poly,".png")), rel_path = FALSE)
```

# Internal validation (optimism-adjusted values)

## ICI, E50, E90 and discrimination by subgroup

The optimism-adjusted estimate is apparent performance minus mean paired optimism. The **Optimism (p2.5 - p97.5)** column shows percentiles of the optimism distribution, not a confidence interval for the optimism-adjusted estimate. N is displayed as a whole number; for ethnicity, the underlying N is the mean across imputations.

```{r table-s1}
make_table(internal_table("Female"),
           next_table_caption("Internal validation performance, female model."))
```

```{r table-s2}
make_table(internal_table("Male"),
           next_table_caption("Internal validation performance, male model."))
```

# Instability analysis

## Variation of performance metrics across the bootstrap iterations (test performance)

The following tables show the 2.5th, 50th and 97.5th percentiles of test performance across the bootstrap iterations. These percentiles describe variation in performance when models developed in bootstrap samples were evaluated in the corresponding original imputed datasets. They are not confidence intervals for the optimism-adjusted estimates.

```{r test-performance-variance-female}
female_variance_table <- variance_percentiles[
  variance_percentiles$Gender == "Female",
  c(
    "Metric",
    "2.5th percentile",
    "50th percentile",
    "97.5th percentile"
  ),
  drop = FALSE
]

make_table(
  female_variance_table,
  next_table_caption(
    "Distribution of test performance across bootstrap iterations, female model."
  )
)
```

```{r test-performance-variance-male}
male_variance_table <- variance_percentiles[
  variance_percentiles$Gender == "Male",
  c(
    "Metric",
    "2.5th percentile",
    "50th percentile",
    "97.5th percentile"
  ),
  drop = FALSE
]

make_table(
  male_variance_table,
  next_table_caption(
    "Distribution of test performance across bootstrap iterations, male model."
  )
)
```
